# From Rental Cars to Robotaxis: Hertz’s Bet on Fleet Operations

**From:** The AV Market Strategist <avmarketstrategist@substack.com>  
**Date:** 2026-10-29T14:41:59.000Z

---

View this post on the web at https://avmarketstrategist.substack.com/p/from-rental-cars-to-robotaxis-hertzs

Every robotaxi still has to be charged, cleaned, repaired and financed. Hertz built a separate company to do that work, and it starts with human drivers.
Doria Holbrook is CEO of Oro Mobility, the fleet platform Hertz launched this year to own, operate and orchestrate vehicles for ride-hail and autonomous platforms. Before Hertz, she worked at Cruise and helped build Amazon’s last-mile delivery network. Oro runs a 45,000-vehicle rideshare fleet across 33 US markets and works with Lucid, Nuro and Uber on its first autonomous fleet in the Bay Area.
First, the origin. I asked why Hertz spun Oro out instead of keeping it in-house, what makes innovation inside a hundred-year-old company hard, and where the name comes from.
Then the model. Doria explains why Oro treats its driver-led fleet as the precursor to driverless operations, what an AV company actually buys from Oro, how pit stops differ from depots, and where Oro draws the line on remote assistance.
Then the operations: what the Atlanta pilot taught the team, which KPIs partners measure, and why years of maintaining a large EV fleet transfer to autonomous vehicles.
Then the money: what the $80 million strategic investment will fund, how Oro sets itself apart from other fleet operators, and why the missing residual-value market makes autonomous vehicles hard to finance.
It ends with Europe, Hertz’s franchise network, and what success looks like for Oro over the next five years.
